messages:
Marta: quick follow-up to the canary RFC — I sketched a small pattern I want us to adopt: "satellite canaries". idea: small dedicated pods in the same infra slice as tenants that run a lightweight variant + an explicit handshake (probe + signed token) before traffic is routed. we need a clear router <-> satellite contract so fallback is simple and deterministic.

Alex: short q — why satellites vs mirrored traffic to staging? latency + cold-start realism. satellites let us exercise locality, KV cache warmups, and edge kernel paths without affecting primary capacity.

Sam: sounds reasonable. interface thoughts: router should treat satellite as a first-class backend with states: UNVERIFIED, WARM, ACTIVE, DEGRADED. transitions only via probe results and scheduler ack. fallback should be triggered if DEGRADED or UNVERIFIED after n failures.

Rachael: +1 on explicit states. also we must define metrics and sampling: success_rate, median_p95_latency, kv_hit_ratio, model_size_mismatch. keep sampling at 1% of user traffic for production pilot to avoid cost blowup.

Marta: proposed minimal contract (router <-> satellite):

```
POST /handshake
body: { canary_id, epoch, probe_signature }
response: { status: WARM | REJECTED, accepted_epoch }
```

router must only route 'pilot' traffic to satellites after WARM. if handshake fails or satellite reports DEGRADED, router must atomically fallback to primary and emit a single 'swapback' event to tracing.

Cheng: telemetry / logging: please add a single telemetry event `satellite.swapback` with tags { tenant_id, canary_id, reason, probe_latency_ms }. also have `satellite.transition` for state changes. store raw probe traces for 24h by default.

Alex: rollback/playbook question — what are concrete thresholds? I propose: fail > 2 probes within 10s => DEGRADED; p95 latency > (primary.p95 * 2) for 5m => DEGRADED; overall success_rate < 98% over 1m => swapback.

Sam: those look fine but make them parameterized per-tenant. enterprise tenants may want stricter SLOs. config should be per-route and default to conservative values.

Rachael: operational note — we need a safe evacuation path for satellites when node maintenance occurs. scheduler should pre-mark satellites as DRAINING and router must hold traffic until warm replacement is READY, or else swapback.

DeployBot: CI check idea: add an integration that runs a simulated probe harness against a fake satellite implementation and ensures the router treats states properly. job: `ci/satellite-handshake`.

Marta: action items: 1) Sam/Cheng draft the contract proto + metric names 2) Rachael draft operation runbook for swapbacks/drains 3) Alex run threshold sims using replay data 4) I'll own the RFC appendix. ping me if you want to pair on probe signature details. :thumbsup:

Alex: i'll volunteer to run the replay sims later today.

Cheng: will draft the telemetry events and a small logging schema. will post PR with field names.

Rachael: will sketch the runbook and include failure modes (partial kv-eviction, compressor mismatch).

Marta: thanks all — keeping this tight will make rollouts predictable.
